targetAudience.primary: Engineering leads and governance owners responsible for long-lived digital-employee memory
targetAudience.knowledgeAssumption: The reader understands persistent memory, retrieval systems, model upgrades, and operational approval boundaries.
targetAudience.readerProblem: A durable memory store is often treated as safe to inherit after a model or embedding change merely because its files and vector dimensions remain intact.

whyNow: A controlled memory-portability study reports direction-dependent model-swap effects and incomplete recovery from mixed embedding spaces, exposing a migration risk that ordinary storage-integrity checks cannot see.

externalHook.description: The bytes survive the upgrade while the meaning available to the new reader changes.

coreProposition: Physical persistence, semantic compatibility, recoverability, and activation authority are four distinct states; durable memory must be re-admitted after a model, writer, reader, or embedding change before it becomes authoritative for the new runtime.

originalValue.description: Turns a vague compatibility check into four separately evidenced decisions, with migration evidence bound to the exact direction of change.

readerTakeaway: Treat semantic-stack changes as governed migrations: preserve provenance, test the exact migration direction, verify a recovery route, and issue a separate activation decision.

supported: The primary study reports strongly direction-dependent performance when one model reads another model's free-form notes.
The study reports that mixing two same-dimension embedding versions recovers only part of the gain from full re-embedding.
The evidence supports separating storage integrity from semantic compatibility and recovery evidence.
unsupported: A claim that all free-form memory is unsafe
A requirement to retain raw history when policy forbids it
General production validation across every model and memory type
uncertain: How small a semantic probe suite can reliably detect harmful drift
How to migrate when raw source cannot be retained
When compatibility evidence should expire after further changes

firstPartyRole.rationale: The argument is derived from public primary research and remains independently useful without any first-party project.

decisionReason: The controlled comparisons support a bounded operational model without overstating general validity.
